correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the all-length proof over F_2. Bit changes toggle Hamming-weight parity; adjacent swaps toggle the parity of the sum of occupied positions and preserve weight. Hence a triangle has exactly one swap. Its endpoints differ in two adjacent bits, so the only valid common one-bit neighbor zeros both (the alternative creates 11). Thus the triangle vectors have private swap-edge coordinates. In the pure-replacement graph take a highest-weight incident vertex of any nonempty even edge set and cancel two downward edges with the square given by deleting both bits. In the potential summing endpoint weights over occupied edges, deleting these two edges and possibly adding the two lower ones decreases the potential by at least four. The squares therefore span, and eliminating swap edges by their triangles leaves a replacement cycle. Connectivity by deletion gives the claimed ranks. Every basis has T_n+B_n members and at most T_n triangles; the weight lower bound is sharp exactly if all triangles are used and every other cycle has length four. Recounting edges by the available positions produces the Fibonacci convolutions. For example, expanding the swap convolution by Binet gives 5 sum_{i=1}^{n-1} F_i F_{n-i}=(n+1)(2F_{n+1}-F_n)-2F_{n+1}; the replacement convolution is the same sum at n+1. Substituting in 3T_n+4B_n gives L_n. For n=1 both ranks and L_n are zero. No finite run is needed for the theorem.
residual_risks: RESULT.md line 49's ancillary count of 1884 replacement squares at n=11 counts checker entries, not distinct squares. Lines 45–49 of verify.py admit both opposite pairs of each square. Each distinct square is identified by a valid top word and a pair of its ones, so there are sum_k binom(11-k+1,k) binom(k,2)=942 distinct squares. Duplicating incidence vectors does not affect either rank check, and the standalone square count is not part of the theorem.
The theorem does not classify which mixed four-cycles can occur in optimal bases or count the optimal bases themselves.

value.rationale: Adding swap edges to a standard constrained-word cube naturally changes the short generators of its cycle space. The exact optimal cost and the necessity of every swap triangle decide how the two move types participate in an optimal basis for all lengths, rather than supplying a finite edge count or only a sampled solution. The constructive decomposition also gives a useful direct method of finding an optimum without searching longer cycles.
residual_risks: Does not enumerate or structurally classify all permitted choices of four-cycles in an optimum.
